hints.title: Append Length Combination Obstacle
hints.text: At each step, you can append either zero '0's or one '1's to a string. How can calculating the number of valid sequences of each specific length between low and high tally all good strings modulo 10^9 + 7?

hints.title: Additive Length Transition Invariant
hints.text: The number of ways to form a string of length L equals the ways to form length L - zero plus the ways to form length L - one.

hints.title: Modular 1D Array Accumulation Procedure
hints.text: Initialize an array of size high + 1 with base case 0 mapped to 1. For each length L from 1 to high, add combinations from L - zero (if L >= zero) and L - one (if L >= one), taking modulo 10^9 + 7. Sum the entries for all lengths from low to high modulo 10^9 + 7 and return the total.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: H: maximum string length high (up to 10^5)
complexity.notes: Iterates through lengths up to H, performing constant work per step.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursive branching takes O(2^H) exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Array of size H + 1 provides rapid lookups for sequence lengths.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Applying modulo arithmetic at each addition step to avoid integer overflow.
